package sample

// Simple has no decisions.
func Simple() int { return 1 }

// Branchy has complexity 5: if, for, case, and one &&.
func Branchy(a, b bool, xs []int) int {
	if a && b {
		return 1
	}
	for range xs {
		switch {
		case a:
			return 2
		default:
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// Deep nests four levels: for, if, switch, if.
func Deep(xs []int) {
	for _, x := range xs {
		if x > 0 {
			switch x {
			case 1:
				if x == 1 {
					_ = x
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// Chain keeps an else-if chain at one level.
func Chain(x int) int {
	if x == 1 {
		return 1
	} else if x == 2 {
		return 2
	} else if x == 3 {
		return 3
	}
	return 0
}

// Wide has a condition with four boolean operators.
func Wide(a, b, c, d, e bool) bool {
	return a && b || c && d || e
}

// Exempt is over the limit on purpose.
// complexity-check:allow a flat dispatch table reads best as one switch.
func Exempt(a, b, c, d, e bool) bool {
	return a && b && c && d && e
}

type T struct{}

// Method has a pointer receiver.
func (t *T) Method() {}
